issues.detail: The Vietnamese 'Nguyền xin Ngài' (Pray/May God) adds a petitionary tone that is not present in the Greek. The Greek 'καταρτισαι υμας' is a simple subjunctive expressing a purpose or result of the preceding context, not a formal prayer or request to God.

The Vietnamese 'là Đấng vinh hiển thuộc về Ngài' (is the glorious one belonging to You) misinterprets 'ω η δοξα' (how glorious/how great is the glory). The Greek expresses an exclamation of praise regarding the glory, not a description of Christ as a possession of God.
